artists.biography: Modest Mouse is an American indie rock band formed in 1993 in Issaquah, Washington, and currently based in Portland, Oregon. The founding members were lead singer/guitarist Isaac Brock, drummer Jeremiah Green and bassist Eric Judy. They achieved critical acclaim for their albums The Lonesome Crowded West (1997) and The Moon & Antarctica (2000) and found mainstream success with the release of Good News for People Who Love Bad News (2004) and its singles "Float On" and "Ocean Breathes Salty". The following album We Were Dead Before the Ship Even Sank (2007) brought additional successes with the single "Dashboard".

Modest Mouse.biography: Modest Mouse is an American indie rock band formed in 1993 in Issaquah, Washington, and currently based in Portland, Oregon. The founding members were lead singer/guitarist Isaac Brock, drummer Jeremiah Green and bassist Eric Judy. They achieved critical acclaim for their albums The Lonesome Crowded West (1997) and The Moon & Antarctica (2000) and found mainstream success with the release of Good News for People Who Love Bad News (2004) and its singles "Float On" and "Ocean Breathes Salty". The following album We Were Dead Before the Ship Even Sank (2007) brought additional successes with the single "Dashboard".

perplexity.description:
An Eraser and a Maze is the eighth studio album by American rock band Modest Mouse, released on June 5, 2026, through Isaac Brock’s independent label Glacial Pace Recordings and distributed by Virgin Music Group. Marking the band’s first full-length release in five years following The Golden Casket (2021), the album signifies a significant homecoming to the indie scene after more than 25 years with Epic Records. The 15-track record, spanning 48 minutes and 54 seconds, blends the band’s gritty indie roots from their Up Records era with major-label refinement and later experimental tendencies, all unified by a conceptual framework inspired by a physics theory suggesting the simultaneous existence of past, present, and future.

Produced primarily by frontman Isaac Brock alongside Jacknife Lee, Suzy Shinn, Justin Raisen, and Jeremy Sherrer, the album features a dynamic sonic palette that stretches from propulsive, anthemic classics to stripped, raw moments. Opening with the vibrant single “Picking Dragon’s Pockets” and including the lead track “Look How Far” (which features former Sleater-Kinney drummer Janet Weiss), the record showcases Brock’s trademark raw candor while exploring themes of progress, self-sabotage, mortality, and loss. Critics have noted the album’s ability to feel both familiar and alien, warm and cold, capturing the essence of every era of Modest Mouse happening at once.

An Eraser and a Maze represents Modest Mouse’s first venture on an independent label since their 1997 classic The Lonesome Crowded West, reclaiming creative freedom and embarking on a new era. The album’s tracklist includes standout songs like “Remember Yourself,” a poignant and whimsically meandering piece that encapsulates the record’s reflective tone, as well as experimental entries such as “Rotten Fruit” (featuring Justin Raisen) and “Song About Nothing”. With its innovative blend of genres—spanning indie rock, alternative, and neo-psychedelia—the album has been described as a cohesive sonic space that refuses easy optimism while delivering relatable disarray and moments of brilliance.
